title: Winners, losers as Browns outlast Steelers 27-24 on Thursday Night Football
text:
Are the Cleveland Browns…legit? Cleveland continued its impressive start to the 2026 season with a 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. The Browns had a more commanding 21-10 lead in the third quarter before a late surge from Aaron Rodgers and Co. made things interesting.
From Patrick Mahomes and the undefeated Chiefs visiting the undefeated Raiders to Lions-Panthers on Sunday Night Football, here are five games to watch in NFL Week 4.
Cleveland continued its impressive start to the 2026 season with a 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. The Browns had a more commanding 21-10 lead in the third quarter before a late surge from Aaron Rodgers and Co. made things interesting. But Deshaun Watson led a drive to just get into field-goal range, setting the stage for kicker Andre Szmyt to nail the winner from 56 yards.
Rodgers had one last shot at a Hail Mary in the closing seconds, but the throw did not have the required power and Grant Delpit picked it off. Monken is enjoying an excellent start to his first season as the Browns head coach. Cleveland has rallied off three straight wins for the first time since 2023, taking down Tampa Bay and Carolina prior to today's win.
The defense looks razor sharp and is giving opposing quarterback fits with elite athleticism and speed, while the emergence of youngsters on offense have rejuvenated that side of the ball. Up next is a trip to theThe limitations of a 42-year-old Rodgers were on full display. He did nail some tight throws that were reminiscent of his past, but it was clear he couldn't hang with the physicality of Cleveland's defense -- especially in a tough atmosphere.
Rodgers completed 22 of 40 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns and two picks, including one to seal the game. He was also sacked five times, all by different Cleveland defenders. Pittsburgh has a clear ceiling with Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy as they drop to 2-2. Watson didn't play flawless ball, as he missed some easy targets that could've put the game away sooner.
But he's getting significant help from second-year running back Quinshon Judkins, who rushed for a touchdown on the night and provided six catches from the backfield. The rookie wideout pair of KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston also stood out. Boston led the way with four catches on seven targets for 89 yards, including a 61-yard catch and run. Concepcion caught five passes on eight targets for 64 yards.
And that's before getting into Jerry Jeudy. Cleveland could be building something intriguing. Young teams will show signs of indiscipline -- that was the case with Cleveland in this one. The Browns were penalized a whopping 14 times, costing them 88 yards.
Arguably the biggest one came on a Pittsburgh 4th-and-10 near the end zone. Rodgers' intended pass for Darnell Washington wasn't going to be hit due to tight double-coverage, but rookie defensive back Emmanuel McNeil-Warren got too handsy and was called for a pass interference. It led to a late touchdown. Jared Verse was then called for offsides on the ensuing two-point try.
Rodgers had lined up in the shotgun, but the margins allowed him to QB sneak it in instead to tie the game at 24-24. Verse has to set the tone better as one of the more proven players on the team. It wasn't a pretty first half for the 28-year-old Metcalf, who was finding issues getting open against Cleveland's flying defensive backs.
But he had a sharp turnaround to spark Pittsburgh's comeback, making crucial catches in the second half to give Rodgers a reliable outlet. Metcalf finished with five catches on nine targets for 115 yards, including a 43-yard haul. His limitations on route-running are well known, but this level of impact can be undeniable. A win would've changed the narrative.
From Myles Garrett and A.J. Brown to Mike Evans and Trey Hendrickson, here are some of the biggest NFL stars with new teams heading into the 2026 season.
